newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDEN'S BLOMQVIST JOINS AC MILAN'S FOREIGN STARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN'S BLOMQVIST JOINS AC MILAN'S FOREIGN STARS.

text.p: Swedish forward Jesper Blomqvist has joined AC Milan from IFK Gothenburg, becoming the Italian club's ninth foreign star.

Blomqvist, 22, a Sweden international whose name had been linked with several top European clubs including Barcelona, told a news conference he had settled on AC Milan after playing against them twice for his Swedish club.
"I decided in favour of Milan after the club leadership told me about their way of working and their will to be the best," Blomqvist said.

"All the time I have wanted to play for a big club, or one that is better than Gothenburg, and there were not many to choose from," added Blomqvist, who signed a new contract with Gothenburg only last August.

Blomqvist said money was not the decisive factor and no transfer fee was disclosed, but Italian newspapers have put the transfer figure at between $3 million and $3.5 million, and one report said the player would earn $790,000 a season.
Gothenburg chairman Gunnar Larsson commented: "I can only say that Jesper is the most expensive player we have ever sold."
His home-town club, tiny Tavelsjo, stands to gain one million Swedish crowns ($220,000) from the deal, the Swedish news agency TT reported.

Left-footed Blomqvist's dribbling and assertive style impressed Milan when Gothenburg played Milan twice in European Champions' Cup ties this season. Blomqvist was man of the match when Gothenburg came from behind to win 2-1 at home, and they later lost 4-2 in Milan.
Blomqvist is the fifth Swede to play for AC Milan, following in the footsteps of Gunnar Gren, Gunnar Nordahl , Nils Liedholm and Kurt Hamrin.
He is due to play his last match for Gothenburg on December 4 against Portugal's FC Porto at the Ullevi stadium.

In Milan, he will join a squad which already includes foreign stars George Weah (Liberia), Marcel Desailly and Christophe Dugarry (France), Dejan Savicevic (Yugoslavia), Zvonimir Boban (Croatia), Edgar Davids and Michael Reiziger (Netherlands). Germany's Christian Ziege is also set to join the Italian club.
